content_units: Best Laptop Fit for a CS Student

You want the best balance of   portability + battery life + 16GB RAM   under   $1,200  , with   gaming performance as a lower priority  . Based on those priorities, the   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5   is the strongest fit overall, with the   Acer Swift Go 14   as a close premium alternative.
Rank   Laptop   Price   Weight   Battery   RAM/Storage   Key Trade-off
1   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5     $899       1.46 kg       13 hrs     16GB / 512GB SSD   Best value and battery; less storage than Acer
2   Acer Swift Go 14     $1,099       1.32 kg       11 hrs     16GB / 1TB SSD   Lighter and more storage; costs more and trails Lenovo on battery
3   ASUS TUF A15     $999       2.2 kg       7 hrs     16GB / 512GB SSD   Strongest graphics; fails portability priority
-   Why it ranks first:   It meets every major requirement cleanly: under budget,   under 1.6 kg  ,   16GB RAM  , and the   best battery life   of the three.
- Web dev, IDEs, Docker, light VMs
- 512GB SSD is good, but not as roomy as Acer’s 1TB
- Not the best pick if you later want GPU-heavy gaming or 3D work

-   Why it ranks second:   This is the most premium ultrabook-style option here. It is the   lightest  , still portable, and gives you   1TB SSD  , which is excellent for projects, datasets, and dual-boot setups.
- CS students who want more storage headroom
- General coding, productivity, and modern CPU performance
- Battery is good, but still behind Lenovo’s stated 13 hours
- When to choose it over Lenovo:
- If you value   lighter weight + 1TB storage   enough to justify the extra cost
-   Why it ranks third:   It has the best gaming/graphics capability thanks to the   RTX 3050  , but that is not your main priority.
- Better for GPU-accelerated workloads like some ML, rendering, or CUDA-specific tasks
-   2.2 kg   is well above your preferred weight limit
-   7 hours battery   is much worse for student use on campus
- Bulkier 15.6" form factor is less convenient for commuting
- Only choose this if you expect to game regularly or specifically need dedicated GPU power
It best matches your stated priorities in order:
Best upgrade pick: Acer Swift Go 14
Choose this if you are willing to spend more for:
- A slightly more premium portability-focused setup
Not recommended for your stated needs: ASUS TUF A15
It is a good machine, but it misses two of your biggest priorities:

Using your constraints, the biggest eliminator is portability. That makes the ASUS hard to justify for a CS student unless gaming or GPU work is a real need. Between Lenovo and Acer, Lenovo wins on value and battery, while Acer wins on lightness and storage.
